title: Why the C-019 take too long ?

messages.text: Why the C-019 take too long ?

Sorry for the wait. That delay is my call: C-019 was posted at 08:08Z, but I let the second stack-test phone round run first (08:19-08:26Z), because it uses the same phone and the result decides what the swipe is for. Since then the phone was handed over and is being prepared; I've told the agent to skip the cool-down (not needed for a swipe) and I'm putting its Mac-quiet slot first in line. Page 1 should be ready within about 5 minutes; the console will show Start when it is.
Ok, make C-019 as highest priority. Don't make user wait too long.

Done: C-019 is now top priority. It no longer waits for the Mac to go quiet (that only protects the background recording, not your swipe). From now on, any step that waits for you goes ahead of the phone measurement rounds.
You could update state in the C-019, for me to catch up what're you doing on C-019.

Good idea, doing it. C-019 page 1 is ready now; you can press Start. From now on the agent running a step writes a one-line status into the step itself at every change (what it is doing, and roughly when it will be ready), so you can see it on the step page without asking.
Done, let's investigate, distinguish and design. then plan into improvement. i thinking about the priority of this and token capacity.

Agreed. Plan for "still a bit laggy", kept small on tokens:

1. Investigate (now, no new phone time): map every remaining slow frame of the stacked build from the 16 phone runs we already have: where on the page it happens (which section), how long, how often. Owner: wi-stack (already holds that data). About 20-30 min.
2. Distinguish: group them by cause. Known so far: the "people" section entry (got worse in the stack), the style recalculation in the middle (PR-002 fixes it), the fling area around y 2990 (fwreskip). Anything left over gets one Simulator check to name its cause. Same owner, plus fix-scroll-engine for its area.
3. Design: one short proposal to you listing each remaining cause with expected gain, risk, and cost; you pick the order. No new code before you choose.
4. Then the improvements run in your order, ending with another blind swipe pair.

Priority and tokens: this goes first among the investigations. The phone keeps running the already-planned rounds (PR-001 now) in parallel, since they cost almost no tokens while waiting. I start no new agents for this; parked side topics stay parked. Usage is about 12 % of this window (estimate), so there is room; I'll report it every 30 minutes here in chat.

Step 1 (investigate) is done, from the 16 phone runs we already had. Where the stacked build still has slow frames: (1) the 'people' section entry is the only place it got worse than before, by about 37 ms per scroll; we're finding which added fix causes it (Simulator, running now). (2) the same entry has a second slow frame that both builds share. (3) three smaller spots (around the 'secure payment' section, the very first scroll frame, and the 'people' cards shrinking) whose causes are unknown; one Simulator check covers all three. (4) the fling area around the middle of the page goes to the fwreskip fix. Everything else is small. Next: the Simulator checks, then one proposal to you with each fix's gain, risk and cost so you pick the order.
